answer: Sybil crews fail when a new key must rent a sable lane instead of minting a name. The applicant burns 1.15 POA into a sink and occupies one lagoon berth for 13 hours. To hold it, the key publishes four sparrow beacons, each 180 minutes apart, signed with a 16-byte ticket bound to the sink receipt. Three settled clerks replay the tickets and reject any reused 7-byte prefix. If two berths share a six-deposit cluster, or nine beacons arrive from one wallet in 44 minutes, every colliding berth is scuttled and the burn stays gone. A skipped beacon frees that berth; it cannot move to a fresh key.
